task_3.title: Rename built-in pythonpath plugin to python_path to avoid conflict with pytest-pythonpath
task_3.description: The built-in pytest plugin registered as 'pythonpath' conflicted with the third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin, causing the third-party plugin's 'python_paths' configuration option in pytest.ini to be silently ignored after upgrading to 7.0.0. The internal plugin is renamed from 'pythonpath' to 'python_path' so both the built-in plugin and the third-party plugin can coexist without interference.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the built-in pytest plugin for managing Python path entries does not conflict with the third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin. In version 7.0.0, both plugins competed for the same internal registration name, causing the third-party plugin's 'python_paths' configuration to be silently ignored and resulting in 'module not found' errors for users relying on it.

expectation.grounded: The built-in plugin must be registered under the name 'python_path' in the default_plugins list instead of 'pythonpath'. This allows the third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin to register and function correctly alongside the built-in plugin. The built-in 'pythonpath' ini configuration option must continue to work as before. Plugin enumeration APIs (e.g., via the plugin manager) must reflect the new internal plugin name 'python_path'.
expectation.conceptual: The built-in Python path plugin and the third-party pytest-pythonpath plugin must be able to coexist in the same pytest installation without one shadowing or disabling the other. Users who depend on either plugin's configuration should see both honored without interference.

constraints.grounded: The rename must not alter the behavior of the built-in 'pythonpath' ini configuration option — it must still prepend entries to sys.path as before. The plugin must still be loaded as part of the default plugin set. No other default plugin registrations should be affected. The third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin's 'python_paths' ini option must no longer be silently overridden.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must resolve the naming collision without breaking any existing built-in functionality. Users who do not use the third-party plugin should observe no change in behavior. Users who do use the third-party plugin should regain its expected functionality after upgrading.

behavior: The internal plugin registration name changes from 'pythonpath' to 'python_path' in the default plugins list.
The third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin can now register its own 'pythonpath'-namespaced hooks and configuration without being preempted by the built-in plugin.
The built-in 'pythonpath' ini configuration option continues to function identically, prepending specified directories to sys.path.
Users who have both the built-in feature and 'pytest-pythonpath' installed no longer experience silent 'module not found' errors from the third-party plugin's paths being ignored.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is invoked with the built-in 'pythonpath' ini option configured, the specified directories are prepended to sys.path as expected.
When the third-party 'pytest-pythonpath' plugin is installed alongside pytest, its 'python_paths' ini option is correctly honored and the specified paths are available for imports.
When both the built-in 'pythonpath' ini option and the third-party 'python_paths' ini option are configured simultaneously, both sets of paths are available without conflict.
When listing registered plugins via the plugin manager, the built-in plugin appears under the name 'python_path' rather than 'pythonpath'.
When pytest is run without the third-party plugin installed, the built-in Python path functionality behaves identically to version 7.0.0.

task_1.title: Fix ModuleNotFoundError for importlib.readers on Python 3.9
task_1.description: pytest 7.0.0 introduced a get_resource_reader method on AssertionRewritingHook guarded by Python >= 3.9, but it imported FileReader from importlib.readers which does not exist until Python 3.10. This caused a ModuleNotFoundError when collecting any test module that transitively triggered importlib resource loading on Python 3.9. The fix raises the version guard to Python 3.10 and adds a conditional import path for Python 3.11+ where FileReader moved to importlib.resources.readers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not raise a ModuleNotFoundError when collecting test modules on Python 3.9. In version 7.0.0, importing any test module that transitively triggers importlib resource reader resolution causes a crash with 'No module named importlib.readers' because the AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method was incorrectly enabled for Python 3.9, which lacks the importlib.readers module.

expectation.grounded: The AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method must only be defined when running on Python 3.10 or later, not Python 3.9. On Python 3.10 (up to but not including 3.11), FileReader must be resolved from importlib.readers. On Python 3.11+, FileReader must be resolved from importlib.resources.readers. The method must return a FileReader constructed with a SimpleNamespace wrapping the rewritten module path. On Python 3.9, the method must not exist on the hook, allowing the standard import machinery to handle resource reading without invoking the broken code path.
expectation.conceptual: When running on Python 3.9, the assertion rewriting import hook must not attempt to provide a custom resource reader, since the required module does not exist in that Python version. On Python 3.10 and later, the hook should provide a resource reader using the appropriate import path for the running Python version. Test collection must succeed without import errors across all supported Python versions.

constraints.grounded: The get_resource_reader method must not be defined or callable on the AssertionRewritingHook when running Python 3.9. The fix must not regress resource reader functionality on Python 3.10 or 3.11+, where the method should still correctly return a FileReader-based TraversableResources implementation. The version branching for FileReader imports must correctly distinguish between Python 3.10.x and Python 3.11+.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break test collection or resource loading on any supported Python version. Python 3.9 must gracefully fall back to default import behavior for resource reading. Python 3.10+ must retain the custom resource reader capability with correct module resolution for each version.

behavior: On Python 3.9, the AssertionRewritingHook no longer defines get_resource_reader, preventing the ModuleNotFoundError for importlib.readers.
On Python 3.10 (< 3.11), get_resource_reader imports FileReader from importlib.readers and returns it wrapping the rewritten module path.
On Python 3.11+, get_resource_reader imports FileReader from importlib.resources.readers instead, accommodating the standard library relocation.
Test collection on Python 3.9 that transitively triggers importlib resource loading (e.g., importing pip internals) no longer crashes with a ModuleNotFoundError.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest on Python 3.9 and collecting a test module that triggers importlib resource reading, test collection should complete without raising ModuleNotFoundError.
When running pytest on Python 3.10, the AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method should be available and should successfully return a resource reader for rewritten modules.
When running pytest on Python 3.11+, the AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method should import FileReader from the relocated importlib.resources.readers module and function correctly.
When running pytest on Python 3.9, the AssertionRewritingHook class should not have a get_resource_reader method defined.

Given a test file that imports a package triggering importlib resource resolution (e.g., pip._internal), when collected by pytest on Python 3.9, it should not produce an ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError related to importlib.readers.

task_2.title: Restore UnitTestFunction.obj to return unbound method, fixing teardown crash
task_2.description: In pytest 7.0.0, a regression caused TestCaseFunction.obj to return a bound method (attached to a newly created instance) instead of an unbound method. This triggered a TypeError crash during failed test teardown when the unittest TestCase class defined a non-default __init__ requiring positional arguments, because pytest internally attempted to instantiate the TestCase without providing those arguments. The fix restores the pre-7.0.0 behavior by overriding _getobj in TestCaseFunction to retrieve the test method directly from the parent class rather than from a new instance.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that TestCaseFunction.obj returns an unbound method rather than a bound method, preventing an INTERNALERROR TypeError crash during failed teardown for unittest TestCase subclasses whose __init__ requires additional positional arguments beyond the default. This is a regression fix for behavior that changed in 7.0.0.

expectation.grounded: TestCaseFunction._getobj must return the test method obtained via getattr on the parent collector's class object (self.parent.obj) using self.originalname, yielding an unbound method. This avoids calling newinstance() on the parent, which would invoke the TestCase's __init__. When a unittest TestCase has a custom __init__ with required positional parameters and a test within it fails, pytest must not raise a TypeError or INTERNALERROR during teardown or report generation. The _prunetraceback and pytest_runtest_makereport hooks must complete without crashing when accessing item.obj on such TestCaseFunction items.
expectation.conceptual: Accessing the test function object on a unittest-based test item must return the method without creating a new TestCase instance. This ensures that pytest can safely generate failure reports and prune tracebacks for tests in TestCase subclasses with custom constructors, without encountering internal errors.

constraints.grounded: The override must be scoped to TestCaseFunction only and must not alter the obj/_getobj behavior of regular Function items in class-based (non-unittest) test collections. The returned method must still correctly reference the original test method name (originalname) so that traceback pruning via Code.from_function and get_real_func continues to work. The parent assertion (self.parent is not None) must be maintained.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must only affect unittest-style test items and must not change how standard pytest test functions or class-based test methods resolve their callable objects. Existing traceback reporting and failure representation functionality must remain intact for all test types.

behavior: TestCaseFunction.obj now returns an unbound method retrieved directly from the TestCase class, not a bound method from a new TestCase instance.
Accessing TestCaseFunction.obj no longer triggers instantiation of the TestCase class, avoiding TypeError when TestCase.__init__ requires positional arguments.
Failed teardown in unittest TestCases with non-default __init__ no longer causes an INTERNALERROR during report generation.
Traceback pruning (_prunetraceback) for unittest test items completes successfully because obj resolves without raising.
The behavior of regular (non-unittest) Function.obj is unchanged and continues to return a bound method.
acceptance_criteria: When a unittest TestCase subclass defines __init__ with required positional arguments (e.g., test_method) and a test in that class fails, pytest must produce a normal FAILED report without any INTERNALERROR.
When accessing .obj on a TestCaseFunction item, the result must be an unbound method (a function attribute of the class), not a bound method of an instance.
When a unittest TestCase with a default __init__ has a failing test, teardown and reporting must succeed as before with no behavioral change.

When a standard (non-unittest) class-based test method is collected as a regular Function, .obj must still return a bound method attached to an instance, confirming no regression in non-unittest behavior.

When _prunetraceback is invoked on a TestCaseFunction for a failed test in a TestCase with custom __init__, it must not raise TypeError and must correctly resolve the real function for traceback display.

task_4.title: Fix running tests by node ID when parametrize portion contains '::'
task_4.description: When users invoke pytest with a specific test node ID whose parametrized portion (the part inside square brackets) contains '::' characters, pytest failed to collect and run the test. The '::' separator used to delimit module, class, and function parts of the node ID was being incorrectly applied inside the parametrize brackets, causing the argument to be split into too many parts and the test to not be found. The fix ensures that only '::' separators outside of the parametrize bracket portion are treated as node-id delimiters.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest can correctly resolve and run tests specified by node ID when the parametrized portion (inside square brackets) contains '::' characters. Previously, running a command such as 'pytest path/to/test.py::test_name[:::]' would result in 'collected 0 items' and a 'not found' error, because the '::' inside the brackets was misinterpreted as a node-ID separator.

expectation.grounded: The resolve_collection_argument function must partition the test node ID so that '::' delimiters inside the parametrize bracket portion (text after the opening '[') are not treated as path/node separators. When a user passes a node ID like 'module.py::test_func[value::with::colons]', the function should correctly identify 'module.py' as the file path, 'test_func' as the test name, and '[value::with::colons]' as the intact parametrize ID. The test must be collected and executed successfully, with no UsageError or 'not found' error raised for valid parametrized IDs containing '::'.
expectation.conceptual: When a user runs a specific parametrized test whose parameter value contains '::' characters, pytest should correctly identify and execute that test. The node-ID delimiter '::' should only be interpreted as a structural separator for module/class/function boundaries, not within the parametrized value portion of the test identifier.

constraints.grounded: Node IDs without parametrize brackets (no '[' present) must continue to be split on '::' exactly as before. Node IDs with parametrize brackets but no '::' inside the brackets must also behave identically to before. The fix must not alter how as_pypath resolution or fspath construction works. UsageError must still be raised when the resolved path does not exist or when a directory path is paired with selection parts.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not affect the behavior of any test invocations that do not involve '::' inside parametrized brackets. All existing node-ID resolution semantics, including error handling for invalid paths and directories with selection parts, must be preserved.

behavior: When a test node ID contains '[', the argument is partitioned at the first '[' before splitting on '::'. Only the portion before '[' is split on '::', and the bracket portion is reattached to the last split segment.
A node ID like 'test_file.py::test_func[:::]' is now correctly parsed as path='test_file.py', parts=['test_func[:::]'], instead of being incorrectly split into four separate parts.
Tests whose parametrize values contain '::' are now successfully collected and executed when specified by full node ID on the command line.
The 'not found' error and 'collected 0 items' result no longer occur for valid parametrized test IDs that contain '::' in their parameter values.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs pytest with a node ID whose parametrize portion contains '::', such as 'path/to/test.py::test_name[:::]', the test is collected and executed successfully.

When a user runs pytest with a node ID whose parametrize portion contains multiple '::', such as 'test.py::test_func[a::b::c]', the parametrize value is preserved intact and the correct test is found.
When a user runs pytest with a standard node ID without brackets (e.g., 'test.py::TestClass::test_method'), the behavior is unchanged and the test is resolved correctly.
When a user runs pytest with a parametrized node ID that does not contain '::' inside brackets (e.g., 'test.py::test_func[value]'), the behavior is unchanged.
When a user provides a non-existent path as a node ID, a UsageError is still raised regardless of bracket content.
When a user provides a directory path with selection parts, a UsageError is still raised regardless of bracket content.

task_5.title: Delay diamond inheritance warning so it respects standard warning filters
task_5.description: In pytest 7.0.0, the PytestWarning about Item subclasses that also inherit from Collector (diamond inheritance) was issued at class definition time via __init_subclass__. Because this happened before pytest had configured its warning filter machinery, users could not suppress or filter the warning using standard filterwarnings settings in pytest.ini. This made test output excessively noisy for projects using plugins (e.g., pytest-black, pytest-flake8) that had not yet adapted to the new node-type separation. The fix defers the warning to instance creation time so that the pytest warning filter infrastructure is active and can process the warning according to user-configured filters. A per-class deduplication mechanism is also introduced to prevent the warning from being emitted once per test item instance.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the PytestWarning about diamond inheritance (Item subclass also being a Collector) can be suppressed or filtered using standard warning filters configured in pytest.ini or command-line options. Previously, this warning was emitted at class definition time, before pytest's warning filter infrastructure was initialized, making it impossible for users to silence it via filterwarnings settings.

expectation.grounded: The diamond inheritance PytestWarning emitted by the Item class must be issued during Item.__init__ (instance creation) rather than during __init_subclass__ (class definition). The warning must pass through the standard Python warnings machinery at a point when pytest's warning filters (configured via the filterwarnings ini option or -W command-line flag) are already active. A per-class deduplication mechanism via a class-level attribute must ensure the warning is emitted at most once per offending class, not once per instance. The warning message content, warning category (PytestWarning), and the detection logic (checking if any base class is a subclass of Collector) must remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: The diamond inheritance warning must be emitted at a lifecycle stage where pytest's standard warning filter configuration is already in effect, allowing users to suppress, ignore, or escalate the warning using the same mechanisms they use for any other warning. The warning should still appear at most once per offending class to avoid flooding test output.

constraints.grounded: The warning must still be emitted as a PytestWarning when an Item subclass has bases that are also Collector subclasses. The detection logic (iterating cls.__bases__ and checking issubclass(base, Collector)) must remain functionally equivalent. The warning must not be emitted more than once per class across all instances of that class. The warning must not be emitted at import time or class definition time. Existing filterwarnings configurations that target this PytestWarning pattern must now correctly suppress or transform the warning.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not remove or weaken the diamond inheritance diagnostic itself — only change when it is issued. The warning must remain filterable through all standard pytest warning filter mechanisms. The deduplication behavior must not suppress the warning entirely for a class that has never been warned about before.

behavior: The diamond inheritance PytestWarning is no longer emitted when a subclass of Item is defined (class definition / import time).
The diamond inheritance PytestWarning is emitted when the first instance of an offending Item subclass is created during test collection.
After the first instance of a given offending class triggers the warning, subsequent instances of the same class do not re-emit it.
Warning filters configured in pytest.ini filterwarnings, pyproject.toml, or via the -W command-line flag can now match and suppress this PytestWarning.
If a user configures an 'ignore' filter for the diamond inheritance PytestWarning pattern, the warning is fully suppressed in test output.
If a user configures an 'error' filter, the warning is raised as an exception at first instance creation rather than at class definition.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin defines an Item subclass that also inherits from a Collector (e.g., File), and the user configures 'ignore::pytest.PytestWarning' in pytest.ini filterwarnings, then no diamond inheritance warning appears in test output.

When a plugin defines an Item subclass that also inherits from a Collector, and no warning filter is configured, then the PytestWarning is emitted once during test collection (not at import/class-definition time).
When multiple test items of the same offending class are collected, the diamond inheritance warning is emitted at most once for that class.

When the user configures a filterwarnings rule matching the diamond inheritance message pattern (e.g., 'ignore:.*is an Item subclass and should not be a collector.*:pytest.PytestWarning'), the warning is correctly filtered.

When the user configures 'error::pytest.PytestWarning' in filterwarnings, the diamond inheritance warning is raised as an exception during first instance creation, not silently at class definition time.
